subject: Capacity reprice proposal and retro allocation
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@brightbeam.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Delgado <marco@brightbeam.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity reprice proposal and retro allocation

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward. We had a difficult production week and will need short-term uplift in token capacity for the next three weeks while we migrate a model variant. Before we pull the trigger we'd like to understand two things:

- Can Redwood provide a temporary quota reallocation for the period 2025-03-15 to 2025-04-05?
- If we go over our committed window, what is the retro credit/true-up path? We need predictable accounting for our SRE and finance teams.

We can share daily usage exports. Ideally we’d like a blend of a short-term fixed uplift plus a retro credit against overrun so our ARR forecast stays clean.

Attaching our high-level migration plan for context.

Cheers,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of ML Ops, BrightBeam AI
elena@brightbeam.ai

Attachment: BrightBeam_Migration_Plan.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@brightbeam.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity reprice proposal and retro allocation

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the context and the migration plan. We can do a short-term capacity reallocation and offer a structured true-up. High level proposal:

- Temporary uplift: +40% quota on your primary model route from 2025-03-15 through 2025-04-05.
- Billing: uplift billed at pay-as-you-go (PAYG) during the window to preserve commit math.
- Retro allocation: after the window we calculate the overrun and apply a one-time credit equal to 50% of the incremental PAYG spend, applied to the subsequent invoice as an ARR-protected credit.

This approach keeps your committed ARR intact while providing immediate headroom and a predictable reconciliation. Two asks from our side:
1) please upload the daily usage CSV (template attached) so our SRE and pricing engine can sanity-check expected peaks;
2) confirm whether you need rate-limit increases on the inference endpoint (QPS) in addition to token quota. QPS increases require short lead time for routing changes.

I’ve attached the usage template. If that structure looks okay I’ll loop in finance for a quick approval and draft an amendment for your legal team.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: BrightBeam_Usage_Template.csv (text/csv)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@brightbeam.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, accounting@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Mar 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity reprice proposal and retro allocation

Looping in a proposed commercial alternative for finance to review:

Olga — thanks for the sensible structure. For BrightBeam I suggest we offer an alternative "credit ladder" option that may be cleaner for accounting:

- Increase quota by +40% for the same window (2025-03-15 to 2025-04-05).
- Rather than a single 50% retro credit, convert the expected incremental PAYG into a three-month amortized credit applied as 30% of the incremental spend per month (months 1-3), capped at the actual incremental spend.
- If usage during the window remains within the +40% uplift, no further charge. If it exceeds the uplift, the excess is billed PAYG and eligible for the same amortized credit policy.

Rationale: stretches credit recognition across quarters which BrightBeam finance flagged as a preference. Karthik — does accounting need an explicit PO amendment or can we proceed with an emailed signed amendment and DocuSign?

Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena@brightbeam.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity reprice proposal and retro allocation

Thanks Olga and Jordan — this looks workable. BrightBeam prefers the amortized credit ladder (Jordan’s alternative) to keep our Q2 ARR clean. Two quick confirmations:

- We’ll take the +40% uplift for 2025-03-15 through 2025-04-05 with the three-month amortized credit at 30% per month.
- We need a modest QPS increase on the inference endpoint from 120 to 180 QPS during the uplift window. Please confirm routing lead time; we need it by 2025-03-14 EOD.

I attached the signed amendment draft to expedite DocuSign. If Redwood can confirm the QPS routing by tomorrow morning we’ll proceed.

Best,
Elena

Attachment: BrightBeam_Signed_Amendment_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
